headline: Strike starts at Teck's big Highland Valley copper mine
detail: About 1,200 Steelworkers walked out Saturday at Canada's largest open-pit copper mine after talks failed; Teck is running at reduced capacity. A long strike would tighten North American copper supply and support copper and scrap prices.

headline: Copper bounces back Friday after hitting a five-week low
detail: COMEX copper rose about 1.7% Friday to roughly $6.51 a pound and London copper gained 1.8% as the tech-stock selloff eased. Still, LME stocks climbed to 273,750 tons, which keeps a lid on rallies.

headline: Fed meets Tuesday–Wednesday; hold expected, December hike still likely
detail: Traders expect no change Wednesday but see about a 79% chance of a December hike, with PCE inflation due Thursday. A hawkish message would firm the dollar and weigh on metals.

headline: Mills expected to pay more for ferrous scrap in November
detail: Dealers and mills told SMU November prices will probably rise after October settled $20–30 a gross ton higher once low opening bids failed to bring in material. Busheling averaged about $480/gt in October.

headline: London copper slips Monday as warehouse stocks keep building
detail: LME three-month copper eased about 0.6% to near $14,240 early Monday with stocks at the highest since July, mostly metal landing in North American warehouses. Marex called the backdrop bearish.

headline: Houthi strikes on Saudi oil sites push Brent to a four-year high
detail: Attacks on Saudi energy sites drove Brent above $116 Friday, its highest in over four years, before it eased Monday on hopes of US-Iran de-escalation. High oil feeds inflation worries and rate-hike bets that hurt metals.

headline: Alsip-area yard bids ease a penny on copper
detail: MetalRecap's south-suburb averages show #1 copper at $4.75 and #2 at $4.59 a pound, each down a cent, with heavy steel and sheet iron steady at about 9 cents a pound. Big Daddy and Central Metal left posted prices unchanged.

headline: Cleveland-Cliffs posts best quarter in three years, sees bigger 2027
detail: Cliffs swung to a third-quarter profit on higher steel prices and guided fourth-quarter EBITDA to about $715 million and 2027 above $4 billion. Strong steel margins keep mills buying scrap.

headline: Gold drops about 4% on the week to a three-month low
detail: Spot gold fell to about $3,995 Friday, its worst week since June, as high oil and rate-hike bets hit non-yielding metals. It edged back above $4,000 early Monday.

headline: Silver sinks to lowest since last November
detail: Silver fell about 6% on the week to near $54, down almost 20% this year, pushing the gold-silver ratio above 74. Silver is more tied to industry and rates, so it is falling harder than gold.

headline: Platinum and palladium stay near multi-month lows
detail: Platinum is down about 10% in a month near its lowest since July, and palladium is near its lowest in over a year on auto-sector worries. That means lower converter payouts.

headline: Converter buyers average about $90 a unit
detail: A national converter buyer lists an average of about $90.15 per converter, with large foreign cats $90–$450, based on platinum near $1,565, palladium $1,054 and rhodium $8,800.

headline: Nickel drops 1.6% as study group now sees a surplus
detail: LME nickel fell to about $15,865 Friday after the International Nickel Study Group flipped its 2026 forecast from a deficit to a small surplus. That weighs on stainless scrap values.

headline: LME aluminum is down about 21% since its June peak
detail: London aluminum has slid from about $3,855 in early June to $3,043 on Friday on oversupply worries, even with low stocks. Aluminum scrap bids have followed it lower.

headline: Iron ore holds near $91 as China port stocks dip
detail: Iron ore 62% edged up to about $90.83 Friday as stocks at China's main ports fell 550,000 tons and hot metal output rose. Prices remain near two-year lows.

headline: China's copper stocks drain as import premium hits 11-year high
detail: Shanghai exchange copper stocks fell more than a quarter last week to about 54,000 tons and the Yangshan import premium hit its highest since 2014. Strong Chinese buying helps offset the US stock build.

headline: China's state buyer strikes annual iron ore deal with Rio Tinto
detail: China Mineral Resources Group reportedly reached a new yearly supply deal with Rio Tinto after pausing talks in August. Centralized buying gives China more pricing power and can keep iron ore prices low.

headline: October car sales on track for a flat 15.6 million pace
detail: J.D. Power expects October US new-vehicle sales of about 1.33 million, a 15.6 million annual rate, flat with last year, with hybrids at 18.6%. Steady builds keep auto scrap like busheling flowing.

headline: Ford reports Wednesday after aluminum supply hit
detail: Ford posts third-quarter results Oct. 28; the Novelis aluminum disruption is costing it about $1.5 billion this year and supplier problems paused some F-150 lines in September.

headline: GM to close its Brownstown battery plant near Detroit
detail: GM is shutting the Michigan battery pack plant, where staffing had already shrunk to under a dozen, as it pulls back on EVs. Slower EV builds mean less copper demand but more hybrid and converter demand.

headline: Data centers lift construction spending as building costs jump
detail: August construction spending rose 0.9% with data-center work up over 70% in a year, while homebuilding fell 4.8%. Construction input prices are up 11.2% from a year ago, including steel and copper wire.

headline: New-home sales due Tuesday as mortgage rates dip to 7.32%
detail: September new-home sales come out Tuesday; the 30-year mortgage rate fell to 7.32%, its first weekly drop since late August. Housing has been the weak spot for steel and copper demand.

headline: US-Mexico trade deal stalls over 50% steel and aluminum tariffs
detail: Talks hit a wall over cutting Section 232 duties on steel, aluminum and metal products, and big progress may wait until after the Nov. 3 elections. The tariffs keep US steel and aluminum prices above world levels.

headline: US factory gauge hits a 53-month high
detail: S&P Global's flash manufacturing PMI rose to 56.0 in October, the strongest in over four years. Good for metal demand, but it also strengthens the case for another Fed hike.

headline: Southern Copper posts record profit, sees slight copper surplus
detail: Southern Copper's quarterly profit jumped 63% on high prices, but copper output slipped 1% and management expects a small global surplus this year. A surplus view argues against a big copper rally.
